title: quantization-nan-debug-scratchpad-maya-2026-03-07
content:
Scratchpad: NaN / quality regression when switching to INT8 (and sometimes FP8) with zeta-3b model.

Summary / symptom:
- Intermittent NaNs in logits during decode with int8-quantized model.
- Behavior: first few tokens are fine, then at some step softmax returns NaN and generation stops (or torch throws RuntimeError: value nan in loss).
- Observed more frequently with long contexts (>1024) and with KV cache enabled.
- BF16 runs OK, FP32 OK. FP8 sometimes reproduces depending on exponent config (e4m3 vs e5m2).

Environments tested:
- Local dev (A100 40GB, CUDA 12.1, torch 2.2.0), small infra node (p4d-like).
- Repro script: repo: tools/quant-repro/run_repro.py (model.load_quantized(...), generate loop with max_new_tokens=256).

Commands tried (most recent):
1) baseline FP32 (stable):
   python run_repro.py --model zeta-3b --dtype fp32 --max_new_tokens 256 --seed 42
2) bf16 (works):
   python run_repro.py --model zeta-3b --dtype bf16 --max_new_tokens 256 --seed 42
3) int8 (failing often):
   python run_repro.py --model zeta-3b --quantize int8 --qtype per_channel --calib_steps 200 --max_new_tokens 256 --seed 42
   -> NaN at step ~37 (non-deterministic, reproducible ~60% with same seed)
4) fp8 attempt (flaky):
   python run_repro.py --model zeta-3b --quantize fp8 --fp8-config e4m3 --max_new_tokens 256
   -> some runs fine, others NaN (fp8 slightly more stable than int8 but flaky)

Observed logs / stack snippets:
- Runtime error when loss computed: RuntimeError: value nan in loss.
- Traceback (trimmed):
  File "/home/maya/projects/quant-repro/runner.py", line 143, in step
    logits = model.forward(input_ids, past_key_values=past)
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1190, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
  RuntimeError: value nan in loss
- Dumped intermediate activations show inf/NaN in attention scores (pre-softmax). Example: attention_logits[12, :, :] contains 1.2e+38 or nan.

Hypotheses / notes:
- Quant scale mismatch: per-tensor vs per-channel scales could create extreme scale values for small-magnitude weights -> overflow in matmul -> huge logits.
- KV cache accumulation: casting cached keys/values to lower precision (int8 path) and accumulating across steps leads to drift/growth and eventual overflow.
- Rotary embeddings / position encoding interactions: rotary uses float sin/cos; quantization might zero small values or introduce large relative errors at high positions.
- Softmax overflow due to very large logits; FP8 sometimes helps because of exponent range (e4m3 > int8 dynamic), but not consistent.
- Calibration distribution not representative: clip thresholds too tight; outliers saturate and blow up downstream when rescaled.

What I tried / observations:
- Calibration steps: 200 -> frequent NaN; 2000 -> fewer NaNs but still occasional.
- Per-channel quantization reduces NaN frequency vs per-tensor.
- Symmetric quantization slightly better than affine with zero_point in our tests.
- Enabling float32 accumulation (in GEMM / matmul) reduces failures; need to verify which kernels used (triton vs cutlass) and accumulation flags.
- Clipping activations pre-softmax prevents NaN (band-aid) but heavily alters outputs.
- Deterministic algorithms (torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)) reduces variance but doesn't remove NaN.

Repro artifacts / scripts:
- tools/quant-repro/repro_int8_nan.py -> minimal loop to trigger NaN, dumps attention_logits to repro/artifacts/ for analysis.
- artifacts contain .npy dumps of: attention_logits_step_*.npy, kv_stats.json (mean/std per-layer), weight_scale_hist.npy.
- Add quick script to compare scales: tools/quant-repro/inspect_scales.py (per-layer histograms).

Immediate next steps (todo):
- Add guard checks in runtime: after matmul, check for inf/nan and log layer id + max/min values (fast path to fail loudly).
- Force float32 accumulation in GEMM for int8 path and run 1000 repro runs to see stability.
- Instrument KV cache: log norm of keys/values each step to see drift pattern.
- Try per-channel symmetric quant + larger calibration dataset (logs from prod prompts, ~5k).
- Run targeted test where rotary embeddings are replaced with identity (sanity check) to isolate if position rotations cause amplification.
- Try fp8 with e5m2 config (larger exponent) to compare stability.
- Cross-check with reference CPU matmul in float32 after dequantize to confirm whether problem originates pre or post-gemm.

Questions / things to ask folks:
- @Ethan: can you dump kernel selection logs for the failing runs? suspect some matmuls falling back to less-precise kernel.
- @Diego: can you re-run calibration with 5k prod-ish prompts and push new scales?
- @Runtime team: how do we force float32 accumulation on A100 kernels in our runtime (cutlass/triton flags)?

Notes from quick chat with Diego (2026-03-07 15:10):
- Diego saw similar NaN on a separate model variant (zeta-6b) but only when sequence length >2048 and with long chat histories. Thinks cache accumulation is probable.
- Suggested to try incremental decode with periodic re-centering of cache (re-encode every N tokens) as mitigation to test hypothesis.

Related artifacts / tickets:
- JIRA INF-1284: quantization NaN incidents (linked).
- GH PR#842: changes to per-channel quant routine (might be related).
- confluence: quantization-playbook (doc with calibration best-practices).

Short log of experiments (chronological):
- 2026-03-05: initial repro on zeta-3b int8, frequent NaNs.
- 2026-03-06: tried per-channel and symmetric quant -> improvement but still flaky.
- 2026-03-07: instrumented dumps and verified attention logits blow up; asked runtime/kernel owners for accumulation flags.
- 2026-03-08: increased calibration to 2k steps; run longer batch of 200 runs overnight (results pending).

Notes-to-self:
- Keep repro seed consistent but expect nondeterminism from kernels.
- When attaching artifacts to ticket, include small nparrays for attention logits (masked to first 128 steps) to keep upload size small.
- If we find root cause near KV accumulation, consider short-term mitigation: rebase KV to float32 after every N steps or use running mean subtraction to prevent drift.

Bottom line: plausible root causes: (1) poor calibration/clipping producing extreme scales; (2) accumulation/precision loss in KV cache; (3) kernel selection/accumulation type causing reduced dynamic range. Next actions: instrument more, force float32 accumulation, larger calibration, and isolate rotary/kv effects.
content_short: Notes + commands for debugging NaN in INT8/FP8 quantization; reproducible on zeta-3b; hypotheses: scale mismatch, kv-cache accumulation, softmax overflow; calibration and per-channel help partially; next steps: instrument kernels, force float32 accumulation, larger calib set.
